issue.title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode
issue.body:
This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-0993a5919b3d7142/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-001b9e9fc72533ca-1778965588668/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-2ec29cdb1234b93b/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-191617d9aacf4dda-1778968860546/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-9ab18f0ac1bd118a/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-38a8fc72b0b8bf03-1778963822341/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-86056579c19c7d6b/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-67233258b489ccf1-1778953271893/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-6905287da7c22b40/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-8895520341e426aa-1778963822341/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-2f158f453558779e/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-b2b9bfa6ac855313-1778965587405/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

This crate provides featureful and fast printers that interoperate with the
[`grep-searcher`](https://docs.rs/grep-searcher)
crate.

# Brief overview

The [`Standard`](struct.Standard.html) printer shows results in a human
readable format, and is modeled after the formats used by standard grep-like
tools. Features include, but are not limited to, cross platform terminal
coloring, search & replace, multi-line result handling and reporting summary
statistics.

The [`JSON`](struct.JSON.html) printer shows results in a machine readable
format. To facilitate a stream of search results, the format uses
[JSON Lines](https://jsonlines.org/)
by emitting a series of messages as search results are found.

The [`Summary`](struct.Summary.html) printer shows *aggregate* results for a
single search in a human readable format, and is modeled after similar formats
found in standard grep-like tools. This printer is useful for showing the total
number of matches and/or printing file paths that either contain or don't

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-e090828df99374fc/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-b360573242cfdaf4-1778965586151/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine

issue.title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode
issue.body:
This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-651a8b6ec81412e8/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-b53a075a894cedf9-1778953267102/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

issue.body:
This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

To facilitate a stream of search results, the format uses\\n[JSON Lines](https://jsonlines.org/)\\nby emitting a series of messages as search results are found.\\n\\nThe [`Summary`](struct.Summary.html) printer shows *aggregate* results for a\\nsingle search in a human readable format, and is modeled after similar formats\\nfound in standard grep-like tools. This printer is useful for showing the total\\nnumber of matches and/or printing file paths that either contain or don't\\ncontain matches.\\n\\n# Example\\n\\nThis example shows how to create a \\\"standard\\\" printer and execute a search.\\n\\n```\\nuse std::error::Error;\\n\\nuse grep_regex::RegexMatcher;\\nuse grep_printer::Standard;\\nuse grep_searcher::Searcher;\\n\\nconst SHERLOCK: &'static [u8] = b\\\"\\\\\\nFor the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock\\nHolmeses, success in the province of detective work must always\\nbe, to a very large extent, the result of luck. Sherlock Holmes\\ncan extract a clew from a wisp of straw or a flake of cigar ash;\\nbut Doctor Watson has to have it taken out for him and dusted,\\nand exhibited clearly, with a label attached.\\n\\\";\\n\\n# fn main() { example().unwrap(); }\\nfn example() -> Result<(), Box<Error>> {\\n    let matcher = RegexMatcher::new(r\\\"Sherlock\\\")?;\\n    let mut printer = Standard::new_no_color(vec![]);\\n    Searcher::new().search_slice(&matcher, SHERLOCK, printer.sink(&matcher))?;\\n\\n    // into_inner gives us back the underlying writer we provided to\\n    // new_no_color, which is wrapped in a termcolor::NoColor. Thus, a second\\n    // into_inner gives us back the actual buffer.\\n    let output = String::from_utf8(printer.into_inner().into_inner())?;\\n    let expected = \\\"\\\\\\n1:For the Doctor Watsons of this world, as opposed to the Sherlock\\n3:be, to a very large extent, the result of luck. issue.body:
This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-0f0520aefb6651fb/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-c1a38306ed49dc1c-1778962528364/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

AddMessageTool { msg: "{\"ok\":true,\"file_path\":\"/home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-0f0520aefb6651fb/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-c1a38306ed49dc1c-1778962528364/BurntSushi/ripgrep/crates/matcher/src/lib.rs\",\"exists\":true,\"byte_len\":45841,\"start_line\":1,\"end_line\":400,\"truncated\":true,\"content\":\"/*!\\nThis crate provides an interface for regular expressions, with a focus on line\\noriented search. The purpose of this crate is to provide a low level matching\\ninterface that permits any kind of substring or regex implementation to power\\nthe search routines provided by the\\n[`grep-searcher`](https://docs.rs/grep-searcher)\\ncrate.\\n\\nThe primary thing provided by this crate is the\\n[`Matcher`](trait.Matcher.html)\\ntrait. The trait defines an abstract interface for text search. It is robust\\nenough to support everything from basic substring search all the way to\\narbitrarily complex regular expression implementations without sacrificing\\nperformance.\\n\\nA key design decision made in this crate is the use of *internal iteration*,\\nor otherwise known as the \\\"push\\\" model of searching. In this paradigm,\\nimplementations of the `Matcher` trait will drive search and execute callbacks\\nprovided by the caller when a match is found. This is in contrast to the\\nusual style of *external iteration* (the \\\"pull\\\" model) found throughout the\\nRust ecosystem. There are two primary reasons why internal iteration was\\nchosen:\\n\\n* Some search implementations may themselves require internal iteration.\\n  Converting an internal iterator to an external iterator can be non-trivial\\n  and sometimes even practically impossible.\\n* Rust's type system isn't quite expressive enough to write a generic interface\\n  using external iteration without giving something else up (namely, ease of\\n  use and/or performance).\\n\\nIn other words, internal iteration was chosen because it is the lowest common\\ndenominator and because it is probably the least bad way of expressing the\\ninterface in today's Rust. As a result, this trait isn't specifically intended\\nfor everyday use, although, you might find it to be a happy price to pay if you\\nwant to write code that is generic over multiple different regex\\nimplementations.\\n*/\\n\\n#![deny(missing_docs)]\\n\\nuse std::fmt;\\nuse std::io;\\nuse std::ops;\\nuse std::u64;\\n\\nuse crate::interpolate::interpolate;\\n\\nmod interpolate;\\n\\n/// The type of a match.\\n///\\n/// The type of a match is a possibly empty range pointing to a contiguous\\n/// block of addressable memory.\\n///\\n/// Every `Match` is guaranteed to satisfy the invariant that `start <= end`.\\n///\\n/// # Indexing\\n///\\n/// This type is structurally identical to `std::ops::Range<usize>`, but\\n/// is a bit more ergonomic for dealing with match indices. In particular,\\n/// this type implements `Copy` and provides methods for building new `Match`\\n/// values based on old `Match` values. Finally, the invariant that `start`\\n/// is always less than or equal to `end` is enforced.\\n///\\n/// A `Match` can be used to slice a `&[u8]`, `&mut [u8]` or `&str` using\\n/// range notation. e.g.,\\n///\\n/// ```\\n/// use grep_matcher::Match;\\n///\\n/// let m = Match::new(2, 5);\\n/// let bytes = b\\\"abcdefghi\\\";\\n/// assert_eq!(b\\\"cde\\\", &bytes[m]);\\n/// ```\\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Hash, PartialEq)]\\npub struct Match {\\n    start: usize,\\n    end: usize,\\n}\\n\\nimpl Match {\\n    /// Create a new match.\\n    ///\\n    /// # Panics\\n    ///\\n    /// This function panics if `start > end`.\\n    #[inline]\\n    pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Match {\\n        assert!(start <= end);\\n        Match { start, end }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Creates a zero width match at the given offset.\\n    #[inline]\\n    pub fn zero(offset: usize) -> Match {\\n        Match { start: offset, end: offset }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Return the start offset of this match.\\n    #[inline]\\n    pub fn start(&self) -> usize {\\n        self.start\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Return the end offset of this match.\\n    #[inline]\\n    pub fn end(&self) -> usize {\\n        self.end\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Return a new match with the start offset replaced with the given\\n    /// value.\\n    ///\\n    /// # Panics\\n    ///\\n    /// This method panics if `start > self.end`.\\n    #[inline]\\n    pub fn with_start(&self, start: usize) -> Match {\\n        assert!(start <= self.end, \\\"{} is not <= {}\\\", start, self.end);\\n        Match { start, ..*self }\\n    }\\n\\n    /// Return a new match with the end offset replaced with the given\\n    /// value.\\n    ///\\n    /// # Task id: BurntSushi__ripgrep-2209
Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-9a6ab1dec836e160/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-c30d784dd5ffb231-1778968861003/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-61d55dd069d3feff/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-c9841bdf11e59aee-1778962528370/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Use the repository tools to inspect the code, make the minimal fix, and finish by producing the patch output.

Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208

Repository root: /home/brasides/.ploke-eval/campaigns/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1/prototype1/nodes/node-d7ef74b517cb8238/instance-targets/p1-five-gen-1x3-20260516-1-treatment-branch-ccfbb42e20f22f5b-1778968860686/BurntSushi/ripgrep
Base SHA: 4dc6c73c5a9203c5a8a89ce2161feca542329812
Title: printer: fix duplicative replacement in multiline mode

This furthers our kludge of dealing with PCRE2's look-around in the
printer. Because of our bad abstraction boundaries, we added a kludge to
deal with PCRE2 look-around by extending the bytes we search by a fixed
amount to hopefully permit any look-around to operate. But because of
that kludge, we wind up over extending ourselves in some cases and
dragging along those extra bytes.

We had fixed this for simple searching by simply rejecting any matches
past the end point. But we didn't do the same for replacements. So this
commit extends our kludge to replacements.

Thanks to @sonohgong for diagnosing the problem and proposing a fix. I
mostly went with their solution, but adding the new replacement routine
as an internal helper rather than a new APIn in the 'grep-matcher'
crate.

Fixes #2095, Fixes #2208
